evidence_quote: SEP is an energy-management certification program administered by the DOE that helps facilities implement the ISO 50001 energy-management standard and verify energy savings.

Energy performance indicators (EnPIs) are measured parameters, ratios, or models that help to quantify energy use and efficiency improvements at the organization, facility, system, process, or equipment level.

stage1.ineligibility_reason: Program/framework overview of the U.S. DOE Superior Energy Performance (SEP) certification program and generic ISO 50001 EnMS implementation steps. EnPIs appear only as a generic definition; no specific EnPI/EnB measurement model is presented, proposed, evaluated, or characterised (no variables, functional form, or construction/estimation approach).

paper_type.evidence_quote: Participating facilities can qualify for Silver, Gold, and Platinum designations

stage1.notes: paper_type borderline: DOE 'Superior Energy Performance' program-overview article; coded 'maturity model or framework' (SEP certification framework with Silver/Gold/Platinum maturity tiers), but 'other' (practitioner/promotional program overview) is defensible. Ineligible under v2.3: EnPIs only generically defined, no specific EnPI/EnB model characterised. level_3b='not applicable' per ineligibility, though SEP examples cite chemical process industries.
